company.name: Larsen & Toubro
company.tag: Projects that take years to deliver
company.summary: Engineering, construction and manufacturing activities behind large infrastructure and industrial projects.
company.description: Larsen & Toubro works across engineering, procurement, construction, manufacturing and services. Its projects can include transportation, buildings, water, energy and industrial infrastructure.
company.money: Customers pay as projects and services are delivered. Order intake, execution milestones, working capital, project costs and contract terms determine how orders become revenue, cash and profit.
company.ownership: This profile covers Larsen & Toubro Limited and its consolidated group. Some L&T-associated businesses are separately listed subsidiaries, so study the parent and each listed entity separately.
watch: How much work is contracted, and when is it expected to execute?
Are costs and contract terms supporting profitable delivery?
How quickly do billed amounts and project spending turn into cash?
risks: Delays and cost increases can reduce project profit.
Large public or private customers can affect payment timing.
A large order book is less useful if pricing or contract risk is poor.
update: Orders are the beginning of the story
An order book indicates contracted opportunity. Execution, cost control and collection determine the financial outcome.
company.question: Is L&T’s order book the same as revenue already earned?
company.answer: No. The order book represents work yet to be executed. Revenue is recognised as contractual work is performed under applicable accounting rules.
